# Asian Paints Limited

<!-- Generated by `make client-docs`. Do not edit inside the markers. -->

Researched 2026-09-29 · status **complete** · Budget spent on two full annual-report PDFs (FY2024-25, FY2023-24) plus supporting searches; FY2022-23 statutory breakdown and project-level CSR-2 table were not reached within the 8-search/6-document budget. No PAN/CSR-1/Darpan identifier, no named grants table, and no explicit 'priority' stated_geography list distinct from footprint were located.

Asian Paints Limited (CIN L24220MH1945PLC004598, www.asianpaints.com) is a Section 135-bound corporate CSR spender. No prior catalog record existed, so all findings are new. Statutory CSR annexure data was extracted for FY2024-25 (avg net profit ₹5,437.44 cr, 2% obligation ₹108.75 cr, total spent ₹109.26 cr, impact assessment done via Grant Thornton Bharat LLP and KPMG) and FY2023-24 (avg net profit ₹4,540.36 cr, 2% obligation ₹90.81 cr, total spent ₹91.26 cr, impact assessment via Mott MacDonald, Renalysis/CSR Box, KPMG, Ormax). FY2022-23 is only evidenced by a secondary news source citing ₹77.42 crore total spend; the primary FY2022-23 filing was not reached within budget. Sector-wise CSR spend (Enhancing Vocational Skills/Beautiful Homes Academy, Water Stewardship/Watermark, Health & Hygiene, Disaster Management) was captured for both FY2024-25 and FY2023-24, along with programme descriptions (Beautiful Homes Academy, Watermark, SAFAR, SPARSH), several FY2024-25 output metrics (training reach, health beneficiaries, water potential created), footprint locations tied to water-stewardship interventions (explicit: Narmada district, Gujarat; derived state for Khandala, Mysuru, Patancheru, Cuddalore, Sriperumbudur, Vizag, Ankleshwar, Rohtak), CSR committee contacts, and the two annual-report documents. No named grant recipients with amounts, PAN/CSR-1/Darpan identifiers, or a project-level CSR-2 style spend table were found; the company points to a CSR Projects webpage for that detail which was not fetched within budget.

## What it set out to find

- identity, identifiers (CIN/domain)
- csr_year figures FY2022-23, FY2023-24, FY2024-25 (avg net profit, prescribed CSR, spend, overheads, impact assessment cost, excess/unspent)
- csr_spend by programme/sector
- footprints (places where CSR actually ran)
- partners (implementing/impact-assessment agencies)
- programmes (Beautiful Homes Academy, Watermark, SPARSH, Safar, etc.)
- metrics (outputs/outcomes for skilling, health, water programmes)
- documents (annual reports / CSR annexures)
- contacts (CSR committee office bearers)
